cands.name: Jamie Forsyth

money.note: Covers January 2023 on, primary and general. Party-committee lines are often in-kind staff and mail.
money.source: Alabama Fair Campaign Practices Act system, downloaded Nov 5, 2026

cands.bio: Jamie Forsyth is a small business owner from Ranburne in Cleburne County. He founded Forsyth Floor Covering in 1990 and has run it for over 35 years. He completed an Advanced Ministry Training degree at Samford University in 2021. He has not held public office.

endorsements.text: Ballotpedia lists voter guide recommendations from Tabitha's List (a Sway voting group run by Tabitha Isner) and Unburdening The Ballot (a Sway voting group run by Tevin Davis).

cands.gaps: His campaign site does not name where he was born, though it says he has lived in Ranburne all his life. We found no stated position from him on data centers, homestead property taxes, limits on out-of-state or institutional land buyers, immigration or H-1B visas, guns, abortion, or taking money from foreign-linked groups. His statements on land, schools and police are general and say nothing on specific bills or policies. He did not complete Ballotpedia's Candidate Connection survey, and we found no news coverage of him or any controversy.

qual.background: He has owned and run Forsyth Floor Covering since 1990, opened a storefront in Ranburne in 1999 and made it an LLC in 2004. He studied business, art and mathematics at Southern Union State Community College and completed ministry training at Samford in 2021. He has held no elected office.
qual.why: A long career as a business owner and manager fits the middle band. There is no record of legislative service, public office, or law or policy work.

slow-growth-protect-land.evidence: His campaign site says he supports preserving farmland, improving water quality, reducing pollution and promoting responsible land use.

school-choice-teachers.evidence: His campaign site says he supports improving teacher pay and investing in local schools. It says nothing about vouchers, charters or school choice.

back-police-order.evidence: His campaign site says he supports law enforcement and first responders through better training, equipment, mental health resources and funding for small-town departments. It does not mention pay, pensions or penalties.

cands.name: Randy Price

money.note: Covers January 2023 on, primary and general. Party-committee lines are often in-kind staff and mail.
money.source: Alabama Fair Campaign Practices Act system, downloaded Nov 5, 2026

cands.bio: Republican state senator for Alabama District 13 since 2018. Former Lee County commissioner and chairman of the Lee County Republican Executive Committee. Small business owner and farmer in Opelika. Attended Southern Union State Community College. Lost a 2014 Alabama House primary.

endorsements.text: 2014 endorsements (from his unsuccessful Alabama House run, not the 2026 race): Alabama Farmers Federation, Alabama Forestry Commission, Business Council of Alabama, Chambers County Farmers Federation, Lee County Farmers Federation. Ballotpedia found no endorsements for the 2026 race.

cands.gaps: We could not find where Randy Price was born or raised, or when he came to Alabama. The pages give no dates for his time as Lee County commissioner or Republican committee chairman. We found no stated positions or documented actions from him on data centers, homestead taxes, land ownership, growth and land protection, immigration and H-1B visas, donor money, policing, guns, abortion, or school choice and teacher pay. He did not complete Ballotpedia's 2022 or 2026 candidate surveys. The only campaign themes on record are from 2014 (opposition to Obamacare and recruiting investors and companies), and they do not address these topics. The list of bills he sponsored did not load, so we could not say what legislation he has carried. We found no documented controversies beyond his July 2020 COVID-19 hospitalization, which is not a controversy.
